_comment: Workspace profile for the WhatsApp Local AI Assistant. Baileys linked-device bridge + local MCP server (stdio) for Claude Desktop/Code. All data stays local; Claude Pro subscription covers the AI cost with zero API billing. Token efficiency is the primary design constraint.
label: WhatsApp Local AI Assistant

metadata.description: Baileys WhatsApp bridge + MCP server that lets Claude Desktop/Code read, search, summarize, and (with approval) reply to WhatsApp messages — fully local, no API cost, token-efficient.

promptProfile:
wa-assistant conventions (this workspace):
- WhatsApp connection uses Baileys (@whiskeysockets/baileys) as a linked device — NO Playwright, NO Chrome, NO browser scraping.
- Session files live in auth_info/ (gitignored). On first run, print QR to terminal via qrcode-terminal. Persist session via useSingleFileAuthState or useMultiFileAuthState from Baileys.
- All DB access through src/store/db.ts singleton (better-sqlite3, synchronous). Never open a second DB connection.
- MCP server uses stdio transport (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk). Entry point: `node dist/index.js --mcp` for MCP mode, `node dist/index.js` for daemon mode.
- send_message tool MUST include a confirmation field in its response: the tool prepares the message but marks it 'pending' — Claude must call a confirm_send tool to actually dispatch it.
- Hard token budgets per Claude call: summarize ≤ 800 tokens out; QA ≤ 600 tokens out; reply suggestions ≤ 200 tokens out per option (3 options max).
- Every Claude interaction must log { operation, tokensIn, tokensOut } to ai_calls table.
- Run the local filter pipeline (src/filter/pipeline.ts) BEFORE any context is built for Claude — if it returns 'skip', no AI call is made.
- Strict TypeScript (strict:true), no `any`, explicit return types on all exports.
- Honor CLAUDE.md in the project root.

seed.title: Baileys WhatsApp client: QR pairing on first run, session persistence in auth_info/, reconnect loop with exponential backoff on connection drop
seed.notes: src/bridge/client.ts. Use makeWASocket() from @whiskeysockets/baileys with useMultiFileAuthState('auth_info'). On 'connection.update': if qr present, print with qrcode-terminal; if connection==='open', log success; if lastDisconnect.error?.output?.statusCode === 401, wipe auth_info and restart (logged-out); otherwise reconnect with backoff (1s→2s→4s→max 30s). Export a getSock() singleton. src/bridge/handler.ts registers the 'messages.upsert' listener and emits normalized MessageEvent objects.

seed.title: SQLite schema + migration system: contacts, chats, messages (FTS5), summaries, ai_calls tables — single db.ts singleton, schema versioning via user_version PRAGMA
seed.notes: src/store/db.ts: open DB at data/wa.db (create data/ if missing), run migrations guarded by PRAGMA user_version. Schema: contacts(id TEXT PK, name, phone, is_vip INT DEFAULT 0, ai_calls_today INT DEFAULT 0, last_reset TEXT), chats(id TEXT PK, name, is_group INT, unread_count INT DEFAULT 0, last_msg_ts INT), messages(id TEXT PK, chat_id, sender, direction TEXT CHECK(direction IN ('in','out')), body TEXT, ts INT, media_type TEXT, ai_processed INT DEFAULT 0), summaries(id INTEGER PK AUTOINCREMENT, chat_id TEXT, summary TEXT, up_to_ts INT, tokens_used INT, created_at INT), ai_calls(id INTEGER PK AUTOINCREMENT, operation TEXT, tokens_in INT, tokens_out INT, created_at INT). FTS5: CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE messages_fts USING fts5(body, content=messages, content_rowid=rowid) — keep in sync with INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE triggers. DB path configurable via WA_DB_PATH env.

seed.title: Message sync pipeline: receive Baileys messages.upsert events, normalize to local schema, dedup by message id, upsert into SQLite — handle text, image captions, and audio (skip body for non-text)
seed.notes: src/bridge/handler.ts. On messages.upsert: for each WAMessage, extract { id: msg.key.id, chatId: msg.key.remoteJid, sender: msg.key.participant || msg.key.remoteJid, direction: msg.key.fromMe ? 'out' : 'in', body: msg.message?.conversation || msg.message?.extendedTextMessage?.text || '', ts: Number(msg.messageTimestamp), mediaType: detect from message keys (imageMessage/audioMessage/videoMessage/documentMessage or null) }. Upsert into messages with INSERT OR IGNORE (dedup by id). Update chats.unread_count and chats.last_msg_ts. For outgoing messages (fromMe), direction='out' and body is the sent text. Emit a NewMessage event for the filter pipeline.

seed.title: MCP server scaffold: stdio transport via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, tool registry, graceful error handling, --mcp CLI flag to boot MCP mode vs daemon mode
seed.notes: src/mcp/server.ts. Create an MCP Server with name='whatsapp-assistant', version='0.1.0'. Register all tools (list_chats, get_messages, get_unread, search_messages, send_message, confirm_send, summarize_chat). Connect via StdioServerTransport from @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/stdio.js. src/index.ts: if process.argv.includes('--mcp') → boot bridge (to receive new messages) + MCP server; else → boot bridge + filter daemon loop. On SIGINT/SIGTERM: close MCP server gracefully, close Baileys socket, flush SQLite WAL (db.pragma('wal_checkpoint(FULL)')), exit 0.

seed.title: Read MCP tools: list_chats (with unread counts + last message preview), get_messages (chat_id + limit + before_ts cursor), get_unread (all chats with pending messages)
seed.notes: src/mcp/tools/list-chats.ts: SELECT id, name, is_group, unread_count, last_msg_ts FROM chats ORDER BY last_msg_ts DESC LIMIT 50. src/mcp/tools/get-messages.ts: params { chat_id: string, limit?: number (default 50, max 200), before_ts?: number }; SELECT from messages WHERE chat_id=? AND ts<before_ts ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT ?. src/mcp/tools/get-unread.ts: SELECT chats.name, messages.* FROM messages JOIN chats ON messages.chat_id=chats.id WHERE messages.ai_processed=0 AND messages.direction='in' ORDER BY messages.ts DESC LIMIT 100. Each tool returns a compact JSON array — never raw message objects, always just { id, sender, body_preview (first 100 chars), ts }.

seed.title: search_messages MCP tool: full-text search across all message bodies using SQLite FTS5 — returns ranked results with chat context, no Claude needed
seed.notes: src/mcp/tools/search.ts. Params: { query: string, chat_id?: string (optional, filter to one chat), limit?: number (default 20) }. SQL: SELECT m.id, m.chat_id, c.name as chat_name, m.sender, m.body, m.ts FROM messages m JOIN messages_fts fts ON m.rowid=fts.rowid JOIN chats c ON m.chat_id=c.id WHERE messages_fts MATCH ? [AND m.chat_id=?] ORDER BY rank LIMIT ?. Sanitize input (strip FTS special chars: * " ( ) OR AND NOT). Return { results: [...], total_found: number }. This is a pure local operation — Claude never needs to call the API just to search.

seed.title: send_message + confirm_send MCP tools: two-step send gate — send_message stages a pending message, confirm_send dispatches it via Baileys after Claude shows the user the draft
seed.notes: src/mcp/tools/send-message.ts: params { chat_id, body }. Returns { pending_id: uuid, chat_name, body, warning: 'Review the message above and call confirm_send(pending_id) to dispatch.' }. Stores pending in a Map<string, PendingSend> in memory (TTL 5 min). src/mcp/tools/confirm-send.ts: params { pending_id }. Looks up the pending message, calls sock.sendMessage(chatId, { text: body }), removes from map, logs to ai_calls. If pending_id not found or expired → error. NEVER auto-confirm — Claude must surface the draft to the user and get approval before calling confirm_send.

seed.title: summarize_chat MCP tool: return an existing summary if fresh (< 10 new messages since last), otherwise generate a new one by sending only the delta + previous summary to Claude
seed.notes: src/mcp/tools/summarize.ts. params { chat_id, force_refresh?: boolean }. Logic: (1) load latest summary from DB; (2) count messages since summary.up_to_ts — if ≤ 10 and !force_refresh, return cached summary immediately (0 tokens); (3) otherwise load messages since up_to_ts (max 100), build a compact string (each line: '[HH:MM sender]: body'), prepend previous summary if exists; (4) return a structured prompt string that Claude should use with its own API call (this tool returns the data, Claude calls itself) — OR call Claude via the CLI adapter in src/ai/client.ts if running in daemon mode. Hard output budget: 800 tokens. Store result in summaries table with created_at and tokens_used.

seed.title: Local routing pipeline: synchronous chain of heuristics that classifies each new incoming message as skip | notify | summarize | reply before any MCP tool is called by Claude
seed.notes: src/filter/pipeline.ts + src/filter/rules.ts. Rules (applied in order, first match wins): (1) direction='out' → 'skip'; (2) is_group=1 AND body doesn't contain @mention of this device's JID → 'skip'; (3) body.length < 5 → 'skip'; (4) contact.is_vip = 1 → 'reply'; (5) question pattern (body ends with '?', or contains מה/האם/כמה/מתי/איפה/who/what/when/where/how) → 'notify'; (6) >= 5 unread messages from this contact → 'summarize'; (7) ai_calls_today >= 10 → 'skip' (rate limit); (8) default → 'skip'. Rate limit resets at midnight (check last_reset date). Result logged to console but never written to DB for 'skip' messages.

seed.title: Claude Desktop config template + Windows startup: claude_config/claude_desktop_config.json template, Task Scheduler XML for auto-start on login, and a one-command setup script
seed.notes: claude_config/claude_desktop_config.json: { mcpServers: { whatsapp: { command: 'node', args: ['<absolute-path>/dist/index.js', '--mcp'] } } }. claude_config/startup.xml: Windows Task Scheduler task that runs 'node <path>/dist/index.js' (daemon mode, NOT --mcp) at user logon, under the user's account, restart-on-failure. claude_config/setup.ps1: PowerShell script that (a) builds the project (npm run build), (b) copies the MCP config to %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json (merging with existing), (c) registers the Task Scheduler task from startup.xml. Document in comments: Claude Desktop must be restarted after config change.

seed.title: Daemon entry point: boot bridge + filter pipeline in background, log new messages with their routing decision, handle SIGINT/SIGTERM gracefully with DB flush
seed.notes: src/index.ts. Two modes: (A) '--mcp' → init DB + Baileys bridge + MCP server via StdioServerTransport (stdout is the MCP channel — no console.log allowed, only console.error for diagnostics); (B) default daemon → init DB + Baileys bridge, subscribe to filter pipeline events, log decisions to stderr. Shutdown handler (SIGINT/SIGTERM/uncaughtException): await sock.logout() or sock.end(), db.pragma('wal_checkpoint(FULL)'), db.close(), process.exit(0 or 1). Never process.exit() without the DB flush — SQLite WAL must be checkpointed to avoid corruption.
